title: Import-surface tests in test_common.py must run in a subprocess to avoid enable_* side effects
answers: why didn't test_import_all_consistency catch the import * failure
how to test wildcard import of sklearn modules
run python snippet in fresh interpreter in sklearn tests
test hidden by experimental enabler imported in test module
body:
sklearn/tests/test_common.py imports `sklearn.experimental.enable_halving_search_cv` at module level, so in-process checks (e.g. `test_import_all_consistency`) cannot see failures that only happen when experimental estimators are not enabled.
`test_wildcard_import_for_public_modules` builds a script of `from sklearn.<mod> import *` for every top-level public module (`pkgutil.iter_modules`, skipping `_`-prefixed, `tests`, `conftest`) and runs it with `sklearn.utils._testing.assert_run_python_script_without_output` in a fresh interpreter.
The script also asserts no `sklearn.experimental.*` submodule got imported as a side effect of the star imports.
Subprocess tests must be marked `@pytest.mark.xfail(_IS_WASM, reason="cannot start subprocess")` (`_IS_WASM` from sklearn/utils/fixes.py).
When adding a new public subpackage or experimental gate, this test will catch `__all__` entries that raise on access.
